title: Everyday verbs
note: A2 everyday verbs · carriers via use[] · quiz_mode sentence_gap (Match is 1-1; Quiz/Type are Czech sentence + English gap) · F9 2026-09-03: was a 92-word alphabetical dump in nine blocks named A2 list 1-9, with sentences for only 22 of the 92. Cut to 36 in four categories; one sentence per verb; intro rebuilt to tiles plus the borrow/lend table. Words already taught earlier (land, plant, please, train, pass, check) dropped outright; the rest are parked in codex/verbs-cuts-2026-09-03.md for redistribution to theme packs. B1/B2 overlap (borrow, improve, solve) kept deliberately: meeting a verb again one level up is recycling. · F9 flags 2026-09-03: realize -> realise. The course is British throughout (shop/film/flat/trousers are the canonical forms in senses.json), so the American spelling was the odd one out. realise/realize added to SYNONYM_GROUPS, so either spelling is graded correct anywhere (James: British mainly, American accepted).

intro.title: You already know
intro.note: You have these verbs already. Now add nine more in each group.
intro.note_cz: Tahle slovesa už znáš. Teď přidáš devět v každé skupině.

intro.title: You will use these words in

rows: borrow — I borrow a book from you.
lend — You lend a book to me.

intro.note: borrow and lend are one verb in Czech and two in English. I borrow a book from you = půjčím si od vás; you lend a book to me = půjčíte mi.
intro.note_cz: borrow = půjčit si (od někoho), lend = půjčit (někomu). Česky jedno sloveso, anglicky dvě.
